## Working Papers

### The Health Returns to School Air Conditioning: Evidence from Summer Ambulance Use in Japan

*Revised and resubmitted at the European Journal of Health Economics.*

This paper studies the health effects of classroom air conditioning in Japan. 
Using administrative data on school-origin ambulance use and quasi-experimental 
variation in public-school air-conditioning installation, I examine whether 
improved access to cooling reduces adverse health events among school-age children.

### Electricity Prices, Temperature, and Ambulance Use: Evidence from a Tariff Hike in Japan

This paper examines whether increases in regulated electricity tariffs affect 
home-origin ambulance use in Japan. I further study how the health response 
varies with outdoor temperature, providing evidence on the health consequences 
of energy affordability and household adaptation to heat.

### Housing Energy-Efficiency Standards and Temperature-Related Morbidity: Evidence from a Regional Reclassification in Japan


## Research Agenda

My broader research agenda lies at the intersection of health and environmental economics. 
I am particularly interested in how climate, energy costs, housing conditions, 
and other features of environment shape health and adaptation.
